title: RBAC v2 decision service + enforcer sidecar for API/runtime/console
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a centralized RBAC v2 decision service (decision API) paired with an enforcement sidecar pattern for the API gateway, runtime inference service, and Redwood Console. This ticket covers the core evaluation engine, policy format, enforcement contract, audit enrichment, and SSO/SAML attribute mappings so teams can adopt consistent role semantics with minimal integration effort.
acceptance_criteria: Decision API accepts request context and returns allow/deny + obligations within 5ms P50 for cached lookups
Enforcer sidecar integrates with API gateway and runtime process; on deny returns 403 and records structured audit event
Console calls use same decision API and map console actions to RBAC predicates; existing console roles map to new RBAC v2 without loss of privileges
Audit events include actor, effective roles, policy_id, inputs, decision, and cache_hit boolean and are emitted to the audit pipeline
SAML/SSO attribute mappings support role, org, and custom claims; admin flag mapping documented
Fail-closed default behaviour configurable per environment (prod default = fail-closed); fallback mode for non-production documented
Performance regression tests added to CI and perf budget gates (latency + QPS under target workload)
tasks: Design policy schema (attributes, role hierarchy, obligations) and publish JSON Schema
Build decision-service prototype (REST/gRPC) with pluggable store for role & policy data
Implement enforcer sidecar library (Go) and HTTP middleware for API gateway and runtime
Console integration: map UI actions to predicates and add UI for role inspection
Audit enrichment: wire decisions into structured audit events and route to existing audit pipeline
SSO/SAML: add mapping layer for SAML assertions to internal role claims and document mapping rules
Add unit/integration tests and performance bench harness; add CI perf checks
Run security review and threat model; address RBAC bypass and replay risks
implementation_notes: Decision service will be a lightweight, horizontally scalable stateless API backed by a distributed cache + eventual consistency datastore for policies
Adopt attribute-based rules with optional role shortcuts to support legacy console roles; policy evaluation returns obligations for logging and soft-deny flows
Sidecar enforcer favors a small runtime dependency and communicates with decision API over mTLS; use protobufs for low-latency payloads
Cache TTL tuned per policy; include cache invalidation hook for immediate rollouts (webhook/event bus)
Default security posture = fail-closed; provide emergency 'maintenance mode' that allows operators to set temporary permissive policy with explicit audit trail
Keep the policy format engine-agnostic so future runtime in-process evaluators can compile policies locally for ultra-low-latency paths
